name: Rejuran HB

lead: Rejuran HB is a polynucleotide injectable used by clinicians as a skin booster.
The sources reviewed contain no human trials, only a rabbit study on accidental intra-arterial injection.

paras: Polynucleotides are chains of nucleotides; skin booster products inject them into the skin. Specific mechanisms for Rejuran HB were not described in the sources reviewed.
The rabbit study examined vascular behaviour of polynucleotide products after intra-arterial exposure; human safety data were not found.

studies.title: Intravascular behavior of cutaneous polynucleotide injectables following intra-arterial exposure.

lead: Rejuran HB is a polynucleotide (PN) injectable used in aesthetic medicine as a skin booster. Polynucleotides are chains of nucleotides, and the term covers DNA and RNA, which also have uses beyond cosmetics.[1] Rejuran products are referred to in the literature as part of a family that includes Rejuran S and Rejuran HB Plus.[2]

The only published study identified in the sources reviewed is an animal experiment on what happens when polynucleotide products are accidentally injected into an artery. No human clinical studies of Rejuran HB were found in those sources.
infobox: Rejuran S, Rejuran HB Plus, Conjuran

paras: No studies found. A 2026 controlled rabbit study (not a human study) compared intra-arterial injection of PN products of differing viscosity, including Rejuran S, Rejuran HB Plus and Conjuran, with saline and cross-linked HA, examining blood flow and cutaneous consequences.[2]

The rabbit study was motivated by the increasing use of PN injectables and the need to understand their behaviour if injected into a blood vessel.[2] Its findings cannot be directly applied to humans.
